findings.text: The authors used plasmid templates to express tagged enzymes in yeast and checked the affinity-purified preparations by gel electrophoresis. Results specifies “freshly purified Ima proteins.” The Introduction identifies duplicated loci that “encode the same protein.” The cloning paragraph identifies which locus supplied the assayed construct.

The Methods distinguish the isomaltose readout, coupling “the release of glucose and the production of NADPH,” from nitrophenol release with the chromogenic substrate. The substrate specificity table labels the rates “Specific activities (μmol/min/mg).” Each natural-sequence preparation hydrolyzed isomaltose. The concentration curves showed “a clear inhibition at high substrate concentration.” Maltose served as an inhibitor in a separate isomaltose assay.

The strain archive returns enzyme-class links for the named proteins. The exact-reaction lookup returned no accession links. The entries corresponding to the duplicated loci have matching protein sequence digests. The archive links assay rows to the locus named in the cloning paragraph and gives an empty assay list for its identical counterpart. A shared isomaltose affinity record names multiple accessions in a single entry.

Suggested editorial wording. “Purified recombinant Ima1p, Ima2p, Ima3p and Ima5p hydrolyzed isomaltose in vitro. These proteins correspond to four distinct sequences in the S288C archive. The preparation made from IMA3 also represents the protein sequence encoded by IMA4.” Deng et al. (2014), DOI 10.1016/j.fob.2014.02.004, PMC3953731. Experimental procedures §4.2 specifies “IMA1/YGR287C, IMA2/YOL157C, IMA3/YIL172C, IMA5/YJL216C,” pGEMt-IMAx templates, C-terminal polyhistidine tags and “the yeast strain CEN.PK113-5D.” S288C appears in the Introduction as the reference genome.

Table 2 transcribes the isomaltose specific activities as Ima1p 60 (100), Ima2p 54 (100), Ima3p 7.2 (100) and Ima5p 65 (100), in μmol/min/mg at 100 mM isomaltose, pH 7 and 30 °C. The footnote specifies five independent experiments with SEM ≤10% of the mean. Each parenthesized 100 is the reference for that enzyme’s relative activities on other substrates. The remaining columns are engineered Ima3p variants. Section 4.3 measured initial glucose release through hexokinase and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase, detecting NADPH at 340 nm. Substrate purity was checked by HPAE-PAD (§4.1). α-pNPG was assayed at 5 mM by pNP release at 405 nm. Results §2.4 reports no pNP release with β-pNPG. The pH and temperature activity profiles used pNPG, and melting temperatures came from differential scanning fluorimetry (§4.4, Table 1).

Isomaltose concentration curves covered 3.125–250 mM (§4.5). Figure 1 averaged five independent assays. Table 3 gives separately fitted isomaltose Km values, mean ± SEM in mM, of 17 ± 4 for Ima1p, 17 ± 2 for Ima2p, 37 ± 9 for Ima3p and 13 ± 2 for Ima5p (§2.5). Table 2 records zero activity on maltose for each natural-sequence preparation. Figure 3 and §2.6 compare isomaltose hydrolysis by Ima1p and Ima5p with and without maltose as inhibitor, using three independent assays. Section 2.6 also describes a preliminary acarbose inhibition assay with Ima1p and isomaltose.

S288C archive lookup, taxon 559292, parent-records.json fields exact_reaction, counts and parents. RHEA:68864 describes isomaltose + H₂O = α-D-glucose + D-glucose. The snapshot lists zero accessions directly linked to that reaction and five linked to its enzyme class, EC 3.2.1.10 (oligo-1,6-glucosidase). The five Swiss-Prot accessions are IMA1 P53051, IMA2 Q08295, IMA3 P0CW40, IMA4 P0CW41 and IMA5 P40884. P0CW40 and P0CW41 share the same version-1 protein digest. P53051, Q08295, P0CW40 and P40884 each match three isomaltose rows. P0CW41 has no linked assay rows. The empty list leaves separate IMA4 activity unresolved. Releases were Rhea 142, Swiss-Prot 2026_03 and ENZYME 28-Jan-2026.

In assay_coverage, the accession-linked union contains 107 unique BRENDA entries and zero SABIO-RK entries. Of these, 92 name one accession and 15 group accessions. Eleven explicitly name isomaltose on a substrate-dependent field, ten single-accession entries plus one grouped entry. Fifty-two name another substrate and 44 leave the substrate unresolved. The wider EC index of 367 BRENDA and eight SABIO-RK entries covers all organisms. Snapshot brenda2026.1-sabio20260920-v1.

The six BRENDA identifiers exposed in assay_coverage.examples all start with 3.2.1.10/. The isomaltose entries kcat_km_value/16 (P53051 alone) and km_value/92 (P53051 and Q08295 together) report pH 7 and 30 °C. Count the shared Km entry once. At the same conditions, kcat_km_value/12 names sucrose and P53051, and kcat_km_value/17 names methyl α-D-glucopyranoside and both P53051 and Q08295. The substrate is unresolved for ki_value/15 (P40884 and P53051, pH 7 and 30 °C) and ic50_value/20 (P53051 alone, conditions unspecified). Shared archive attribution and separate preparations in the primary paper are compatible.
